value.text: Four travellers must cross a bridge at night with one torch. At most two cross at a time and a pair moves at the slower person's pace. They take 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes. What is the fastest total crossing time, and what is the schedule?

This is the classic bridge crossing puzzle with crossing times of 1, 2, 5, 10 minutes. The optimal solution: send 1&2 across (2 min), 1 returns (1 min), send 5&10 across (10 min), 2 returns (2 min), then 1&2 cross again (2 min) — totaling 17 minutes.

Given the response needs to be under three sentences, I'll present the schedule concisely and note it beats the naive approach of 19 minutes where the fastest person escorts everyone individually.

The fastest total crossing time is **17 minutes**. The schedule is: 1 and 2 cross together (2 min), 1 returns with the torch (1 min), 5 and 10 cross together (10 min), 2 returns with the torch (2 min), then 1 and 2 cross again (2 min). That adds up to 2 + 1 + 10 + 2 + 2 = 17 minutes, which beats the 19 minutes it takes if the 1-minute traveller escorts everyone.
